        HARDWARE BENCH · MODBUS TCP

        TM172PDG temperature injection

        LOCAL KIT REQUIRED

        Open the multi-sensor bench ↗

        Send a simulated temperature to one writable PLC Status Variable. Your PLC application can select that value in place of the scaled AI1 reading when its local bench permit is enabled.

        1. Download and extractPut the kit on the laptop connected to your TM172PDG bench network.
        2. Start the local bridgeOn Windows, open Start-TM172-Bench.cmd. Requires Python 3.9 or later.
        3. Read, then sendEnter the PLC IP, unit ID, and Status Variable address in the browser window the bridge opens.
        Download TM172 bench kit

        The bridge serves the lab on your laptop and communicates with the PLC over Ethernet on TCP port 502.

        PLC target and simulated temperature

        Use the Address column from Machine Expert – HVAC. The bridge subtracts one to obtain the Modbus offset.

        °F

        Read the Status Variable to verify the connection and mapping before enabling writes.

        PLC setup and AI1 selector example
        1. In a bench copy of the project, enable the TM172PDG Modbus TCP server. In Configuration → Modbus Objects → Status Variables, add SimAI1_Tenths as a writable INT with scale 1 and offset 0. Record its project address.
        2. Keep your real AI1 mapping and sensor scaling. Use a separate AI1_Used value in the sequence, in the same units as AI1_Eng and the configured Modbus point. The PLC-local bench permit starts off.
        AI1_Used := AI1_Eng;
IF BenchPermit_Local THEN
    AI1_Used := INT_TO_REAL(SimAI1_Tenths) / 10.0;
END_IF;

        With equipment disconnected, confirm the raw register value in Online Watch before turning on the PLC bench permit. Turn the permit off when finished. The PLC retains the last test value when you close the browser.
